headline: Insilico Medicine says its AI-designed pain drug beat morphine in tests before human trials, with testing in people as the next step.
score_reason: Potentially important non-opioid painkiller, but company-reported, preclinical and without published data.
importance_line: A safe, non-addictive painkiller would matter to patients and health systems, but the claims come from the company itself, there is no human data yet, and nine in ten drugs that reach human testing fail to win approval, health experts say.
summary: The National reports that Insilico Medicine, an AI drug-discovery company with a research centre in Abu Dhabi's Masdar City, has developed a pill called ISM9528 that it believes could work better than morphine for acute and chronic pain. Alex Aliper, the company's president and co-founder, called a non-opioid candidate that outperforms morphine in preclinical models “unprecedented” and said a full safety evaluation will come in clinical trials.
notes: Read in full from The National. Company claims only; preclinical stage. Category left at the default RES (AI drug discovery research); HEA is the alternative.
